primary_content.text: Hi I’m looking for information regarding requirements for retiring to Thailand for a single UK citezen, at time of receiving the UK state pension in two and a half years time. What income and savings do I need?

I’ve seen the new profesional LTR Visa for 10 years, and can see that medical insurance needs to be shown as one requirement, is the pension paid from the UK an accepted income amount, I’m likely to have reasonable savings too. Any advice gratefully received at this stage please. Regards Alan Meadows
Thank you for your message, and we’re glad to assist with your plans to retire in Thailand.

As a single UK citizen approaching retirement age and expecting to receive your UK state pension in a couple of years, you have two main visa options: the Thailand Retirement Visa (Non-Immigrant O or O-A) and the newer Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa for retirees.

The Retirement Visa is ideal for individuals aged 50 and over. To qualify, you must meet one of the following financial requirements: have at least 800,000 THB in a Thai bank account, a monthly income of at least 65,000 THB (your UK state pension can count toward this), or a combination of savings and income totaling 800,000 THB annually. If you apply for the O-A visa, you’ll also need to show proof of health insurance with minimum coverage amounts required by Thai immigration.

The LTR Visa is a newer 10-year visa aimed at wealthy retirees. To be eligible, you must also be at least 50 years old and have an annual income of at least USD 80,000. If your income falls between USD 40,000 and USD 80,000, you may still qualify if you have investments in Thai property or securities. This visa also requires health insurance coverage of at least USD 50,000, or alternatively, a deposit of USD 100,000 in a Thai bank account maintained for 12 months.

Since you mentioned having reasonable savings and a steady pension, it’s very likely you could meet the requirements for either visa, depending on your exact situation when you apply. For more detailed guidance, please feel free to explore our resources the Thai Retirement Visa Requirements page, or get in touch with a Thai visa consultant for personalized advice.

main_topic.h_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand (LTR Visa Thailand) is designed to attract “high-potential foreigners” looking to relocate to Thailand by offering a convenient immigration solution and valuable, exclusive benefits. This makes the LTR Visa in Thailand ideal for foreigners with assets to invest, pensions to spend, or professional skills they can utilize to contribute to Thailand’s economic growth.

If this sounds like you and you’re looking for a way to settle in Thailand for the long term, the LTR Visa makes it easy. The application process for an LTR Visa in Thailand is more complex than those of most other Thai visas, but the perks you get once you have it make building a life in Thailand more convenient, and in some cases, more profitable.
This page will explain Thailand’s Long-Term Resident Visa, who is eligible, what criteria must be met for each type, and how you can apply for one.
Why apply for a LTR Visa Thailand in the first place? Learn why this is one of the most popular visas for expats on our page about the LTR Visa Thailand benefits.

urls.anchor_text: LTR Visa Thailand benefits

main_topic.h_title: Who is Eligible for a Thailand LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Before you can start applying for the LTR Visa, you have to pick one of the categories or “streams” that best apply to you. The LTR Visa comes in four types, each for a specific group of expats:
Wealthy Global Citizens : Investors with significant assets to contribute to Thailand’s economy.

urls.anchor_text: Wealthy Global Citizens

primary_content.text: Wealthy Pensioners : Retirees with high passive income who want to spend their golden years in paradise.

urls.anchor_text: Wealthy Pensioners

primary_content.text: Work-from-Thailand Professionals : Remote workers and “digital nomads” who want to make Thailand their base of operations.

urls.anchor_text: Work-from-Thailand Professionals

primary_content.text: Highly-Skilled Professionals : Professionals with specialized experience and skills hoping to work high-paying jobs in Thai sectors targeted for growth.

urls.anchor_text: Highly-Skilled Professionals

secondary_content.text: There is also a fifth category of LTR Visa for Spouses and Dependents, specifically for those accompanying a primary LTR Visa holder.

urls.anchor_text: LTR Visa for Spouses and Dependents

main_topic.h_title: What are the Requirements for Long-Term Resident Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Foreigners who fall into one of the five categories mentioned earlier can apply for the LTR Visa in Thailand, but each stream has unique eligibility requirements and required documentation. Therefore, your qualifications must match the category you are applying for, and you must provide the required documents that category demands.
Here are lists of the requirements for each stream of the LTR Visa in Thailand.

main_topic.h_title: 1. Wealthy Global Citizens
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: If you aren’t planning on working during your time in Thailand and wish to live off the passive income from your investments, this is the stream for you. To qualify, you must:
health insurance policy
OR provide evidence of savings of at least 100,000 USD held in a Thai or overseas bank account for no less than 12 months before the date of application.
Must provide proof of personal income of at least 80,000 USD annually during the period of 2 years prior to the application date.
Must have at least 1 million USD in assets.
Must have an investment of at least 500,000 USD in Thai government bonds, foreign direct investment, or Thai property.

main_topic.h_title: 2. Wealthy Pensioners (Retirees)
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: If you are 50 years of age or older and interested in spending your golden years in paradise, this is the stream for you. To qualify, you must:
health insurance policy
OR provide evidence of savings of at least 100,000 USD held in a Thai or overseas bank account for no less than 12 months before the date of application.

If your passive annual income is less than 80,000 USD but greater than 40,000 USD, you can still qualify provided you can prove that you have invested at least 250,000 USD in Thai government bonds, foreign direct investment, or Thai property.
*Passive income cannot come from employment. Acceptable passive income sources include but are not limited to pensions, rental incomes, capital gains, dividends, and interest payments.

main_topic.h_title: 3. Work-from-Thailand Professionals
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: If you plan to work remotely for a foreign company while living in Thailand as a digital nomad, this stream is for you. To qualify, you must:
Produce an employment contract or service agreement with a business in Thailand or abroad.
Show proof of work experience in one of the targeted industries. You must have a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience gained within 10 years of the application date.

Currently, work for an employer that is a public company on a stock exchange or a private company in operation for at least 3 years with a combined revenue of at least 150 million USD in the last 3 years.

If your passive annual income is less than 80,000 USD but greater than 40,000 USD, you can still qualify provided you have a Master’s degree or above, own significant intellectual property, or receive Series A funding of no less than 1 million USD.
health insurance policy
OR provide evidence of savings of at least 100,000 USD held in a Thai or overseas bank account for no less than 12 months before the date of application.

main_topic.h_title: 4. Highly-Skilled Professional
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: If you have significant qualifications, high-level skills, and/or valuable work experience, this stream will allow you to work in a high-paying position at a Thai company or institution. To qualify, you must:
Produce an employment contract or service agreement with a business in Thailand.
In the case that you have a PhD in a related field or are working for a Thai government agency, this experience requirement is waived.

If your passive annual income is less than 80,000 USD but greater than 40,000 USD, you can still qualify provided you have a Master’s degree in a science or technology field, or you have special expertise relevant to your position.
The annual income requirement is waived if you intend to conduct work in government-operated higher educational institutions, research centers, specialized training centers, or government agencies.
health insurance policy
OR provide evidence of savings of at least 100,000 USD held in a Thai or overseas bank account for no less than 12 months before the date of application.

main_topic.h_title: 5. Spouses and Dependents of Long-Term Visa Holders
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Your spouse and dependent children can acquire their own LTR visas and enjoy all the privileges that you do. Additionally, you can now add an unlimited number of dependents, including parents and other legal family members. To qualify, each family member must:
Your legal spouse with a valid marriage certificate (as of 2024, same-sex marriages are legal and recognized in Thailand).
Your legal child and under 20 years old with proof of your relationship (birth certificate, adoption papers, etc.)
Have a health insurance policy in Thailand with coverage for medical expenses of no less than 25,000 USD.

main_topic.h_title: How to Apply for an LTR Visa in Thailand
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: To apply for Thailand’s Long-Term Resident Visa, you must gather and prepare all the required documents for your chosen category. Keep in mind that missing or incorrectly prepared documents may lead to delays in your application or an outright rejection.

Once your application packet is complete, you must register online with Thailand’s Board of Investment (BOI), the agency that issues this visa. You will have to submit your application through their online portal, then wait. The processing time can be anywhere from 4 to 8 weeks or more depending on the strength of your application. The BOI may request additional documents or clarifications during this time.

urls.anchor_text: Thailand’s Board of Investment

primary_content.text: If you are approved, you will be contacted by the BOI to set an appointment to collect your visa. If you are applying from outside of Thailand, you will collect your visa and travel document from the Royal Thai Embassy in your country of residence.

main_topic.h_title: Things to Keep in Mind After You Have Your LTR Visa
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Once you have your Long-Term Resident Visa in Thailand, you must abide by its conditions or it will be revoked. Here are some things to keep in mind:
You and any dependents on your visa must report the status of your residence with Thai Immigration annually (instead of every 90 days).
Once you have acquired the visa and filed for a work permit application, you are allowed to conduct your work immediately without having to wait for the issuance of the permit.
Your work permit will be void once your LTR Visa is terminated or expires.

main_topic.h_title: Thailand LTR Visa FAQ
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: This website is owned and operated by Siam Legal, and over our 20+ years of operation, our law firm has gotten a lot of questions about Thai visas, and the LTR Visa in particular. Here we’ve compiled a list of some of the most frequent questions clients have.

urls.anchor_text: LTR Visa

main_topic.h_title: 1. Can I apply for the LTR Visa while I’m in Thailand on a different visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes, you can apply for the Long-Term Resident Visa and convert your existing Thai visa, provided you meet the eligibility requirements.

main_topic.h_title: 2. How long does it take to get an LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Typically, the processing takes 4-8 weeks. However, if you are missing documents or there are errors in your application, the BOI might ask for corrections or clarity, increasing your processing time. If you are applying from outside of Thailand, that country’s embassy may also cause delays if they have a high caseload.

main_topic.h_title: 3. What do I do if my LTR Visa application is rejected?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: If your application is rejected by the BOI, there’s no need to panic. You can reapply after you have addressed the reasons for rejection. Siam Legal’s consulting services can help you pinpoint the reason your application failed and ensure it’s fixed the next time you apply, maximizing your chances of approval.

main_topic.h_title: 4. Can LTR Visa holders buy property in Thailand?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Like all foreigners in Thailand, LTR Visa holders cannot buy land in their name, but you can buy condos and houses. You can also enter into long-term leases that give you de facto control over land and the structures built on them. Siam Legal’s property team can help you determine which property you can buy and help you with the purchase or lease process.

urls.anchor_text: Siam Legal’s property team

main_topic.h_title: 5. Can I get a Thai work permit with an LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: That depends on your type of LTR Visa (stream). Work-From-Thailand Professionals, for example, cannot obtain work permits, while Highly-Skilled Professionals can.

main_topic.h_title: 6. Can my dependents work in Thailand if they hold an LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes, your dependents can apply for a work permit after successfully receiving their LTR Visa. However, they must also meet the necessary requirements for employment in Thailand.

main_topic.h_title: 7. Do I need to apply for a re-entry permit if I leave Thailand on an LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: No, the LTR Visa is a multiple-entry visa, meaning you can leave and return to Thailand as needed, provided it is still valid. No extra steps are required, simply show your passport with the visa inside and you can re-enter Thailand. You even get to use the priority lane!

main_topic.h_title: 8. Do I need to report to Thai Immigration every 90 days on an LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: No, one of the most convenient benefits of the LTR Visa is that holders are only required to report to Thai Immigration once a year as opposed to every 90 days as required for most other Thai visa types.

main_topic.h_title: 9. What’s the difference between the Thailand LTR Visa and the Thailand Elite Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: The LTR Visa is aimed more at professionals and active investors in the country. The Thai Elite Visa, available through the Thailand Privilege Program, is geared more toward residents and frequent visitors. It provides visa terms of 5-20 years, offers a mountain of benefits and free perks, and is far easier to qualify for than most other Thai visas, especially the LTR Visa. However, as it is a tourist visa, employment with a Thai company is not permitted, but you can work remotely in Thailand while holding an Elite Visa.

urls.anchor_text: Thai Elite Visa
Thailand Privilege Program

main_topic.h_title: 10. Do I need health insurance to apply for the LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes, all LTR Visa applicants must have health insurance coverage of at least 50,000 USD. This can be from a policy issued from your home country or one in Thailand. Alternatively, you can provide proof that you have 100,000 USD in a Thai bank account to show that you can cover any medical expenses.

main_topic.h_title: 11. Do I need to be employed before applying for the LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes, you need to provide an employment contract if you are applying under the Highly-Skilled Professionals or Work-From-Thailand Professionals stream. However, if you are applying under the Wealthy Global Citizens or Wealthy Pensioners stream, an employment contract is not required.

main_topic.h_title: 12. Do Social Security payments and other government pensions help me fulfill the LTR Visa’s financial requirement?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes, your social security benefits count as part of your income to meet the LTR Visa financial requirements and count as “passive income” if you are applying under the Wealthy Pensioners category. If the amount of the monthly payment is not enough to meet the minimum income requirement, however, you will need to supplement it with other income streams.

main_topic.h_title: 13. I am in a same-sex marriage, does my partner qualify for a dependent LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Yes, as of October 2024, same-sex marriages are legal and recognized under Thai law. By Thai law, same-sex couples enjoy the legal rights and privileges as everyone else, including eligibility for dependent visas such as the LTR Visa.

main_topic.h_title: 14. Which government agencies issue Thailand’s LTR Visa?
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: Unlike most other visas, the Thai Board of Investment (BOI) handles visa issuance for the LTR Visa. This is because this visa was created for economic development, and why when searching for “LTR Visa Thailand” you will see pages from the BOI appear in your results instead of Thai Immigration or other government agencies.

main_topic.h_title: Summary of LTR Visa Thailand
main_topic.main_title: LTR Visa Thailand | Long-Term Resident Visa Thailand
main_topic.author: ThaiEmbassy.com

primary_content.text: New applications for the Thailand LTR visas have been very popular during its first year. The Thailand Board of Investment has attempted to enhance the process to make a smoother process for long term resident LTR visa holders. Thai government agencies desire for more foreign investment into Thailand so we will see this program stay for long term resident visa holders. The LTR visa holder will enjoy the benefits of living in Thailand for the long term under this program.
If you have questions about the LTR visa or planning to reside in Thailand long-term, reach out to us for a consultation.
